extraction.Name: Ernest Bordeaux
extraction.Refused/Protested: No I did not know any better at the time.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: I mortgaged it for $700.00 that is $700.00 is all I got. The mortgage was supposed to be for $1000.00 but the $300.00 went to the man who made the mortgage. The mortgage was afterwards foreclosed. The mortgage was redeemed by my father, who has since died. He gave me $2500.00 for the land.
extraction.Buyer: Pat Navin of White River was the agent and Murphy and McCullough of Winner were connected with it in some way. The mortgage was redeemed by my father, who has since died. He gave me $2500.00 for the land.
extraction.NOTES: Did not ask for patent; was under the impression that they had to take them; at the time patent was issued did not know any better than to accept it; was young and poor and not competent to look after such things; has no home and no land; mortgage was for $1000.00 but only received $700.00 cash, with $300.00 going to the man who made the mortgage; patent delivered by mail in spring of 1920; signed a receipt for it; wife and four children depend on him for support; subscribed and sworn before notary May 14, 1929; notary commission expires 4-28-32
